title: Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Adversarial Attacks

predicted_errors.error_location: References [49] and [50], lines 465-467
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: References [49] and [50] are the identical paper (Y. Xu and P. Ghamisi, 'Universal adversarial examples in remote sensing: Methodology and benchmark', TGRS 60:1-15, 2022), differing only in journal spelling ('IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing' vs 'IEEE Trans. Geosci. Remote Sens.'). Both numbers are cited in the text ([49] at the sensitivity-metric and Mixup-attack references; [50] at the attack-implementation reference), so one paper appears twice in the bibliography.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 2 statement (lines 123-125) vs Appendix C proof, eq (35)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Proposition 2 statement claims κ(S) ≤ exp(R(S)/(2σ_r(S))) + c, but the proof derives ln κ(S) ≤ R(S)/(√2 σ_r(S)²) (eq 35) and says 'after exponentiation, yields (4)'. The two exponents differ in both the constant (1/2 vs 1/√2) and the power of σ_r (σ_r vs σ_r²). Since R(S)=||SᵀS−α²I|| scales like σ² under S→cS, the proof's version R/(√2σ_r²) is scale-invariant (consistent with κ being scale-invariant), while the statement's R/(2σ_r) scales linearly in c — dimensionally inconsistent for a condition-number bound. The '+c' term also appears only in the statement and is never derived. The proof chain (31)→(35) is internally consistent, so the statement is the erroneous element (likely a typesetting slip).

predicted_errors.error_location: Reference [56] (GaLore), line 83
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [56] (Zhao et al., GaLore) is never cited in the text. Line 83 mentions 'gradient projection, e.g., GaLore' without a bracket citation. All other references [1]-[57] are cited at least once; [56] is the only dangling bibliography entry.

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation numbering: (3)→(5) jump; Remarks 1-2 and Prop 2 proof reference 'Equation (4)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Numbered equations run (1), (2), (3), then (5), (6), (7), (8), (9), (10), (11a-c) — no (4) exists anywhere. Yet Remark 1 ('the bound of Equation (4) is not useful'), Remark 2 ('the proper scaling in (4)'), and the Prop 2 proof closing line ('which, after exponentiation, yields (4)') all reference 'Equation (4)'. The label (4) should attach to the Proposition 2 condition-number bound. Note Remark 2's 'proper scaling in (4)' claim only makes sense for the proof's scale-invariant R/(√2σ_r²) form, not the stated R/(2σ_r), reinforcing the Prop 2 discrepancy.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 column headers (UCM and CIFAR blocks)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The column labeled 'Jitter, ε 0.3' actually contains ℓ²-FGSM ε=0.3 results: values 54.96/43.39/53.30 match Figure 4's FGSM ε=0.3 row, and the text (line 73) explicitly calls 54.96 and 43.39 ℓ²-FGSM ε=0.3 values 'see Table 2'. predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 vs Figures 4/5/6 (VGG16 UCM RobustDLRT clean accuracy)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 reports RobustDLRT clean = 94.61±0.35, but Figure 4 (β=0.075), Figure 5 (β=0.2) and Figure 6 (β=0.15) give clean = 92.61, 92.59, 92.14 respectively. The adversarial entries match the figure rows EXACTLY (89.12/78.68/53.30; 88.33/79.81; 90.33/70.12/47.31), so the runs are shared and clean accuracy — an attack-independent quantity — must agree. 94.61 vs 92.61 differs by exactly one digit (~2 points, ~5.7σ), indicating a transcription error.

predicted_errors.error_location: Text line 306 vs Table 4 (compression-ratio claim)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text claims 'an at least 15% higher compression ratio with RobustDLRT than the second best compression method, CondLR [35]'. Table 4 shows RobustDLRT c.r. = 94.35 vs CondLR (τ=0.5) c.r. = 80, i.e. only 14.35% higher — below 15%. Moreover DLRT in the same table has c.r. = 94.58, HIGHER than RobustDLRT's 94.35, so RobustDLRT does not hold the highest compression ratio and the 'second best' compressing method would be DLRT, not CondLR. The claim is internally inconsistent with Table 4's own numbers.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 2 vs Figures 4/5/6 (VGG16 UCM baseline clean accuracy)

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 caption: 'All runs where RobustDLRT surpasses the uncompressed baseline are highlighted.' Four bold entries do NOT surpass their baselines: UCM VGG16 53.30 vs 54.96, 88.33 vs 89.58, 79.81 vs 85.05, and CIFAR VGG11 ℓ²-FGSM ε=0.1 63.82 vs 64.21. predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix C, eq (37) vs (41), Proof of Proposition 3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Testing the flow equation by S−W gives (37): (1/2)(d/dt)‖S−W‖² + β(∇R,S) + ‖S−W‖² = β(∇R,W) — the ‖S−W‖² term has coefficient 1, correct for the stated gradient flow. But (41) writes +(1/2)‖S−W‖² (coefficient 1/2); (41) does not follow from (37). The Grönwall step (41)→(42) is internally consistent with (41) as written, so the slip is at (37)→(41). A correct derivation from (37) would yield e^{2(τ−t)}-type weights, which would not produce the stated estimate (5) as written. Also line 804 says 'Applying (39) and (40) to (36)' when it is (37) that is used.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 7 vs Tables 2 and 4 (CIFAR10 VGG16 clean accuracy)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Same setup (VGG16/CIFAR10, mean over 10 runs): RobustDLRT β=0.15 clean = 88.80 (Table 7) vs 89.35 (Table 4), with c.r. 94.18 vs 94.35; baseline clean = 90.48 (Table 7) vs 89.83/89.82 (Tables 4/2); DLRT clean = 88.58 vs 89.55/89.23. Clean accuracy and compression rate are attack-independent, so identical protocols must agree across tables. Three tables report three different clean-accuracy values for the same trained configuration.

References [7], [18], [26], [34] list no venue, volume, pages, or arXiv identifier (e.g., [34] Nenov et al., '(Almost) smooth sailing', 2024, cited for the MVT-for-logarithms bound — topically plausible but unverifiable without an identifier). Reference formatting is otherwise inconsistent across the list.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 vs Table 2 (VGG16 UCM ℓ²-FGSM ε=0.1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Same claimed setup, different numbers: DLRT c.r. 94.50 / clean 93.50 / ε=0.1 70.00 (Table 1) vs 95.30 / 93.92±0.23 / 72.41±2.08 (Table 2); RobustDLRT 95.90 / 95.00 / 80.00 vs 95.84 / 94.61 / 78.68. predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2, line 73 (singular-value ratio)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The printed singular values 2.7785 and 0.8210 give κ = 2.7785/0.8210 = 3.3843, but the paper reports κ(S) = 3.3844 (off by 1 in the 4th decimal). The baseline check is exact (1.8627/0.9445 = 1.9722). Likely computed from unrounded singular values, but the printed numbers are inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix C, Proof of Proposition 2 (line 764)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the von Szőkefalvi-Nagy inequality [33] 'bounds the variance ... from below by the range'. The classical Szőkefalvi-Nagy (1918) inequality is an UPPER bound: variance ≤ (max−min)²/4. The paper instead uses variance ≥ (σ_1(SᵀS)−σ_r(SᵀS))²/(2r) (eq 32) — a different, valid lower-bound inequality, but not the cited result. Citing [33] for the lower-bound direction is a misattribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: References [9] and [10], lines 402-404
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Soft duplicate: [9] (ICML 2017, PMLR) and [10] (ICLR 2017) are the same work (Cisse et al., 'Parseval networks: Improving robustness to adversarial examples'), listed under two numbers and cited at lines 35 and 89 respectively.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction contribution 1 (line 41) vs Method computational cost (line 227)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction claims 'a more than 10× reduction in both memory footprint and compute cost'. Parameter reduction up to ~94% (~16.7×) supports the memory part, but no compute-cost reduction is quantified anywhere: the Computational cost paragraph only states RobustDLRT is 'asymptotically the same as LoRA', and training runtime is reported as ~25% overhead over DLRT. For low-rank layers O(2nr+r²) vs O(n²) exceeds 10× only for large n; for small layers the factor is far less. The joint compute-cost claim is unsupported/overstated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction (lines 41, 45) vs Results Table 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction claims 'maintaining clean accuracy and adversarial robustness on par with full-rank baselines' and that the regularizer 'neither degrades training performance nor reduces clean validation accuracy'. Table 2 shows RobustDLRT clean accuracy BELOW baseline in several setups (VGG11 UCM 93.57 vs 94.23; ViT-16b CIFAR 94.66 vs 95.42; VGG11 CIFAR 87.97 vs 88.34; VGG16 CIFAR 89.49 vs 89.82). The abstract's own hedge ('some degradation in clean accuracy may occur') contradicts the stronger Introduction claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 5 caption (line 364) vs Table 5 rows
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 5 caption states 'RobustDLRT (β = 0.075)', but the table body rows are labeled 'β = 0.05' for both VGG16 and VGG11. Additionally, VGG11 β=0 c.r. = 95.82 in Table 5 vs c.r. = 94.89 for DLRT VGG11 UCM in Table 2 (VGG16 matches at 95.30). The caption/body β mismatch is a genuine internal inconsistency; the c.r. difference may reflect the black-box retraining setup but is unexplained.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix C, eq (40), Proof of Proposition 3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The chain 2β‖S−W‖‖W‖ + 2β‖W‖² ≤ (1/2)‖S−W‖² + 2β(1+2β)‖W‖² is valid but not tight: Young's inequality 2βxy ≤ (1/2)x² + 2β²y² (optimal split) gives a total of 2β(1+β)‖W‖², not 2β(1+2β)‖W‖². Since 2β(1+2β) ≥ 2β(1+β), the stated estimate (5)/(42) remains a mathematically valid (looser) upper bound, so the constant is suboptimal rather than wrong.

summary: Exhaustive verification (lenient strictness) of 'Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Adversarial Attacks' found 21 error candidates, 12 of them at or above the standard confidence thresholds. The most serious issues cluster in four areas. (1) Math/proofs: the Proposition 2 condition-number bound is stated as κ(S) ≤ exp(R(S)/(2σ_r(S))) + c, but the Appendix C proof derives exp(R(S)/(√2 σ_r(S)²)) — different constant AND different power of σ_r, and only the proof's version is scale-invariant; the bound itself is also never assigned 'Equation (4)' even though Remarks 1-2 and the proof reference it. The Proof of Proposition 3 additionally has a coefficient slip between (37) and (41) (‖S−W‖² vs (1/2)‖S−W‖²) that breaks the derivation chain. (2) Bibliography: references [49] and [50] are the identical Xu & Ghamisi paper listed twice; [56] (GaLore) is never cited in the text; [9]/[10] duplicate Parseval networks; several entries lack venues/arXiv IDs. (3) Table consistency: Table 2's column headers mislabel the 'Jitter ε=0.3' column (actually ℓ²-FGSM) and 'Mixup ε=0.045' column (actually Jitter); clean accuracy — an attack-independent quantity — is reported inconsistently for the same configurations across Table 2, Figures 4/5/6, and Tables 4/7 (e.g., RobustDLRT VGG16 UCM clean 94.61 vs 92.61/92.59/92.14); and Table 2's bold highlighting does not match its 'surpasses baseline' caption for four entries. (4) Claims vs data: the Results assertion of 'at least 15% higher compression ratio than the second best compression method, CondLR' contradicts Table 4's own numbers (94.35 vs 80 = 14.35; and DLRT at 94.58 exceeds RobustDLRT); the Introduction's 'more than 10× reduction in both memory footprint and compute cost' and 'clean accuracy on par with full-rank baselines' are stronger than the reported results support; and Tables 9, 10 and Figure 2 are referenced but never captioned. Multiple high-confidence findings (≥0.85) mandate correction.
